text:
pagerduty: :rotating_light: PAGED: Canary check failed for inference-service (region: us-west-2). Error rate spiked to 12% on canary shard. Please respond.

mira: I'm on it. grabbing context from canary dashboard.

alex: I see a spike in tokenization errors in the canary logs: `RuntimeError: tokenization table mismatch (vocab size 50256 vs 50258)`. That looks like a vocab/merges mismatch between model weights and tokenizer.

jon: Oof. Any chance the deploy pulled a model build with different tokenizer metadata? Last deploy tag was v2026-03-15-weights.

mira: Checking image manifests... looks like the model artifact `inference-model:v2026-03-15` references weights blob sha256:abc123 and tokenizer sha256:def456. On the dedicated store, weights blob points to different commit than the tokenizer blob. Possible build pipeline race.

deploy-bot: Automated canary rollback available. `redwood deploy rollback --service=inference --target=stable --scope=canary` (dry-run).

alex: We should kill the canary traffic first. If the request routing still sends to canary shards we risk customer impact.

mira: Agreed. @sre-oncall can you flip the routing kill-switch for canary shards? runbook step 2.

sre-oncall: On it. `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood.internal/flags/kill-switch -d '{"service":"inference","flag":"canary_traffic","state":"off"}'` -> 200 OK. Canary traffic drained (30s).

jon: Confirming error rate dropped to baseline on stable. But some customers hit 5xx while canary was active. Sam, can CS surface which accounts saw errors?

sam-cs: I have a partial list from alerts: acct-918, acct-217, acct-404. Reached out to account owners with heads-up. They're asking about root cause.

alex: Next steps: 1) roll back canary to previous stable weights (v2026-03-10) 2) disable auto-deploy from model-build pipeline until we validate artifact integrity 3) kick off hotfix build that pins tokenizer/weights together.

mira: Starting rollback now. Running: ```
# rollback canary to stable model tag
redwood deploy rollback --service inference --to-tag v2026-03-10 --scope canary
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued (job id: rb-6789). Estimated completion 2m.

alex: While rollback proceeds, can someone check whether quantization/weight conversion step mutated tokenizer indices? Known issue when pruning scripts reindex tokens.

jon: I'm pulling conversion logs. Found this snippet in conversion pipeline: ```
# convert_weights.sh
python convert.py --vocab-file vocab.json --merge-file merges.txt --prune --out weights-final.bin
# convert prints: "Applied pruning: removed 64 tokens" -> new vocab size 50256
``` That would explain mismatch. Looks like pruning ran in the build accidentally.

mira: Rollback finished, canary nodes now running v2026-03-10. Running smoke tests.

sre-oncall: Smoke tests green on canary after rollback. No tokenization errors observed. Restoring canary traffic holdoff until we validate the pipeline fix.

sam-cs: CS update sent to impacted accounts: short note + ETA for full postmortem. Customers appreciate quick rollback but want timeline.

alex: Creating incident page and assigning followup: root cause likely model build pipeline allowed pruning step to run on release build. Remediation: add artifact integrity checks (hashes for weights+tokenizer), and block deploy if vocab sizes differ. Also add unit test in build to assert vocab_size unchanged unless explicitly requested.

mira: Will file PR to CI with check `assert metadata.vocab_size == tokenizer.vocab_size` and add warning-level alert if mismatch occurs on staging.

jon: For immediate mitigation, I propose we disable auto-promotion of model artifacts into the deploy registry until the CI hash-check is in place.

sre-oncall: Flag toggled: `auto_promote_models` = false.

deploy-bot: Noted. `auto_promote_models` false applied at org-level.

alex: Assigning owners: mira -> build pipeline fix, jon -> conversion script audit and revert unsafe pruning, sam-cs -> customer comms & impact tracking, me -> postmortem draft.

mira: I'll include reproduction steps and sample logs in the PR. Also adding a blocker gate in release pipeline that compares manifest entries for tokenizer/weights.

sam-cs: Customers asked whether any data was corrupted. We confirmed no inference outputs were stored; only live requests failed with 5xx for short window. Communicated that no PII was exposed.

jon: Quick note for postmortem: include exact error lines and the conversion commit (commit: fd12e9) that introduced pruning.

alex: Thanks all. We'll leave this thread open until the CI check is merged and auto-promotion re-enabled. Postmortem deadline: EOD tomorrow.

mira: PR created: https://git.redwood/inference/ci/-/merge_requests/112 (adds vocab_size check).

sre-oncall: Will monitor for 2h. If no regressions, we'll re-enable canary flows and auto-promote.

sam-cs: I'll update the customers after the postmortem.

deploy-bot: Incident tag: INC-2026-0315-weights-mismatch. Severity: P2.

alex: Closing loop: verified rollback removed errors and customer impact limited. Leaving this thread for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
